key_insight: Crystal VAE latents spontaneously separate by elemental family, enabling FamilySpace to control generated crystals’ family composition through targeted latent sampling.
engineering_relevance: Family-level composition control can guide materials discovery toward promising chemical regions without additional optimization such as reinforcement learning.
method: Identify elemental-family structure in atom-wise VAE latent representations.
Assign each family a distinct source component and train a flow with family-matched source–target pairs.
Use a user-specified family template to select the source component for each atom during generation.
evidence_signal: On MP-20 and MPTS-52, FamilySpace reports competitive generation performance and prescribed family-composition matching; selected templates increase the fraction predicted stable or metastable.
watch_item: Predicted stability does not establish experimental synthesizability, and the abstract provides no quantitative effect sizes.
paper_title: FamilySpace: From Emergent Chemical Semantics to Controllable Crystal Generation
